bookInfo.name: New History of the Five Dynasties

title.zh: 卷十 漢本紀第十: 高祖 隱帝
title.en: Volume 10 Later Jin Annals 1: Gaozu, Emperor Yin
title.raw: 卷十 漢本紀第十: 高祖 隱帝 Volume 10 Later Jin Annals 1: Gaozu, Emperor Yin

sentences.zh: 高祖睿文聖武昭肅孝皇帝，姓劉氏，初名知遠，其先沙陀部人也，其後世居於太原。

translations.literal: Gaozu, the Sagely Literary, Sagely Military, Resplendent and Solemn, Filial Emperor—surname Liu, originally named Zhiyuan—his ancestors were of the Shatuo tribe; later generations dwelt at Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu, temple name the Sagely Literary, Sagely Military, Resplendent and Solemn, Filial Emperor, was of the Liu clan and originally named Zhiyuan. His forebears were Shatuo; his family later settled at Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 知遠弱不好弄，嚴重寡言，面紫色，目多白睛，凜如也。

translations.literal: From youth Zhiyuan disliked play; grave and taciturn, his face was purple and his eyes showed much white—he seemed stern and forbidding.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy Zhiyuan shunned childish games. Grave and sparing of speech, with a purple cast to his face and prominent whites in his eyes, he had a chilling presence.

sentences.zh: 與晉高祖俱事明宗，為偏將。

translations.literal: Together with Jin Gaozu he both served Mingzong as deputy generals.
translations.idiomatic: He and Jin Gaozu both served under Mingzong as junior commanders.

sentences.zh: 明宗及梁人戰德勝，晉高祖馬甲斷，梁兵幾及，知遠以所乘馬授之，復取高祖馬殿而還，高祖德之。

translations.literal: When Mingzong fought the Liang at Desheng, Jin Gaozu’s horse armor broke and Liang troops nearly reached him; Zhiyuan gave him the horse he rode, took Gaozu’s horse, covered the rear, and returned—Gaozu was grateful.
translations.idiomatic: At Desheng, when Mingzong battled the Liang, Jin Gaozu’s horse barding gave way and Liang soldiers nearly took him. Zhiyuan handed over his own mount, rode Gaozu’s horse in the rear guard, and brought him off safely. Gaozu never forgot the debt.

sentences.zh: 高祖留守北京，以知遠為押衙。

translations.literal: When Gaozu remained as regent of the Northern Capital, he made Zhiyuan chief adjutant.
translations.idiomatic: While Jin Gaozu held the Northern Capital as regent, he appointed Zhiyuan his chief adjutant.

sentences.zh: 潞王從珂反，湣帝出奔，高祖自鎮州朝京師，遇湣帝於衛州，止傳舍，知遠遣勇士石敢袖鐵槌侍高祖，以虞變。

translations.literal: The Prince of Lu, Congke, rebelled; the Min Emperor fled. Gaozu came from Zhenzhou to the capital, met the Min Emperor at Weizhou, and halted at a relay station. Zhiyuan sent the brave warrior Shi Gan, an iron mace hidden in his sleeve, to attend Gaozu against trouble.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Lu, Congke, rose in revolt and the Min Emperor fled, Jin Gaozu marched from Zhenzhou to the capital and met the Min Emperor at Weizhou, stopping at a post station. Zhiyuan posted the warrior Shi Gan at his side with an iron mace concealed in his sleeve, lest violence break out.

sentences.zh: 高祖與湣帝議事未決，左右欲兵之，知遠擁高祖入室，敢與左右格鬥而死，知遠即率兵盡殺湣帝左右，留帝傳舍而去。

translations.literal: Gaozu and the Min Emperor discussed affairs without reaching a decision; attendants wished to take them by force. Zhiyuan embraced Gaozu and pulled him indoors; Gan fought the attendants and died. Zhiyuan then led troops and killed all the Min Emperor’s attendants, left the emperor at the relay station, and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Talks between Gaozu and the Min Emperor deadlocked, and the emperor’s men moved to seize Gaozu by force. Zhiyuan bundled him into an inner room while Gan grappled with the assailants and was killed. Zhiyuan then led soldiers who slaughtered every attendant of the Min Emperor, left the emperor at the station, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 天福二年，遷侍衛馬步軍都指揮使，領忠武軍節度使。

translations.literal: In the second Tianfu year he was transferred to commander of the palace horse-and-foot guards and made military commissioner of Zhongwu.
translations.idiomatic: In the second Tianfu year he became commander of the palace horse-and-foot guards and military commissioner of Zhongwu.

sentences.zh: 已而以杜重威代知遠領忠武，徙知遠領歸德，知遠恥與重威同制，杜門不出。

translations.literal: Soon after, Du Chongwei replaced Zhiyuan in Zhongwu; Zhiyuan was moved to Guide. Ashamed to share the same rank as Chongwei, he shut his gates and would not go out.
translations.idiomatic: Du Chongwei soon took over Zhongwu in his place and Zhiyuan was shifted to Guide. He was shamed to hold equal rank with Chongwei and refused to leave his residence.

sentences.zh: 高祖怒，欲罷其兵職，宰相趙瑩以為不可，高祖乃遣端明殿學士和凝就第宣諭，知遠乃受命。

translations.literal: Gaozu was angry and wished to strip him of his military post; Chancellor Zhao Ying said it could not be done. Gaozu then sent Duanming Hall academician He Ning to his house to proclaim the imperial will, and Zhiyuan then accepted the order.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Gaozu, furious, meant to remove him from command, but Chancellor Zhao Ying dissuaded him. He Ning of the Duanming Hall was sent to Zhiyuan’s home to read the imperial reassurance, and only then did Zhiyuan take up his duties again.

sentences.zh: 五年，徙鄴都留守。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was transferred to regent of Yedu.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was made regent of Yedu.

sentences.zh: 九月，朝京師，高祖幸其第。

translations.literal: In the ninth month he went to the capital; Gaozu visited his residence.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he came to court, and Jin Gaozu called at his house.

sentences.zh: 六年，拜河東節度使、北京留守。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was appointed military commissioner of Hedong and regent of the Northern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he received Hedong and the Northern Capital regency.

sentences.zh: 七年，高祖崩。

translations.literal: In the seventh year Gaozu died.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year Jin Gaozu died.

sentences.zh: 知遠從高祖起太原，有佐命功，自出帝立，與契丹絕盟，用兵北方，常疑知遠勛位已高，幸晉多故而有異志，每優尊之。

translations.literal: Zhiyuan had followed Gaozu from the rise at Taiyuan and had merit in founding the dynasty. From the time the Outgoing Emperor took the throne, broke the Khitan alliance, and campaigned in the north, he often suspected that Zhiyuan’s achievements and rank were already high and that, with Jin beset by troubles, he harbored a different ambition—yet each time he treated him with exceptional honor.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyuan had stood with Jin Gaozu from the founding at Taiyuan and earned his place among the founders. After the Outgoing Emperor broke with the Khitan and warred in the north, the court often feared that Zhiyuan’s honors had outgrown his loyalty and that Jin’s calamities might tempt him elsewhere—yet he was lavished with ever greater favor.

sentences.zh: 拜中書令，封太原王、幽州道行營招討使，又拜北面行營都統。

translations.literal: He was appointed Director of the Secretariat, enfeoffed Prince of Taiyuan, made campaign repression commissioner on the Youzhou circuit, and later overall commander of the northern campaign headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Director of the Secretariat and Prince of Taiyuan, then campaign repression commissioner for Youzhou and, later, overall commander of the northern field army.

sentences.zh: 開運二年四月，封北平王，三年五月，加守太尉，然王未嘗出兵。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of Kaiyun 2 he was enfeoffed Prince of Beiping; in the fifth month of year 3 he was made Defender Grand Marshal—yet the prince never took the field.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of Kaiyun 2 he became Prince of Beiping; in the fifth month of the third year he was named Defender Grand Marshal. He never led an army in person.

sentences.zh: 契丹寇澶州，別遣偉王攻雁門，敗之於秀容。

translations.literal: The Khitan raided Cangzhou and separately sent the Great King against Yanmen; he was defeated at Xiurong.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan struck Cangzhou they also sent the Great King against Yanmen; Zhiyuan routed him at Xiurong.

sentences.zh: 八月，殺吐渾白承福等族，取其貲鉅萬，良馬數千。

translations.literal: In the eighth month he killed the Tuguhun Bai Chengfu and his clan, taking their wealth in the tens of thousands and fine horses by the thousand.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month he exterminated the Tuguhun leader Bai Chengfu and his kin, seizing vast stores of goods and thousands of fine horses.

sentences.zh: 四年，契丹犯京師，出帝北遷，王遣牙將王峻奉表契丹，耶律德光呼之為兒，賜以木拐一，木拐，虜法貴之如中國几杖，非優大臣不可得。

translations.literal: In the fourth year the Khitan took the capital and the Outgoing Emperor was moved north. The prince sent teeth officer Wang Jun with a memorial to the Khitan; Yelü Deguang called him “son” and granted one wooden staff—a wooden staff, in barbarian custom, is prized as the Chinese prize a seat and staff; only favored great ministers could receive it.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year the Khitan seized the capital and the Outgoing Emperor was taken north. The prince sent Wang Jun, a staff officer, to present tribute to the Khitan. Yelü Deguang addressed him as a son and gave him a wooden staff—in Khitan usage as honored as a Chinese seat and cane, and granted only to ministers in highest favor.

sentences.zh: 峻持拐歸，虜人望之皆避道。

translations.literal: Jun carried the staff back; Khitan who saw it all yielded the road.
translations.idiomatic: Jun returned with the staff, and Khitan along the way stepped aside at the sight of it.

sentences.zh: 峻還，為王言契丹必不能有中國，乃議建國。

translations.literal: When Jun returned he told the prince that the Khitan surely could not hold China, and they then discussed founding a state.
translations.idiomatic: Back at Taiyuan, Jun reported that the Khitan could not long keep the Central Plains, and they began to plan a new dynasty.

sentences.zh: 二月戊辰，河東行軍司馬張彥威等上箋勸進。

translations.literal: On wuchen of the second month, Hedong campaign deputy Zhang Yanwei and others submitted a memorial urging him to take the throne.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen in the second month Zhang Yanwei, deputy to the Hedong campaign staff, and others presented a memorial urging accession.

sentences.zh: 辛未，皇帝即位，稱天福十二年。

translations.literal: On xinwei the emperor ascended the throne and called the era the twelfth Tianfu year.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei Liu Zhiyuan took the throne and kept the era name at the twelfth Tianfu year.

sentences.zh: 磁州賊首梁暉取相州來歸。

translations.literal: Liang Hui, bandit chief of Cizhou, seized Xiangzhou and came to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Hui, a rebel leader in Cizhou, took Xiang prefecture and submitted.

sentences.zh: 武節都指揮使史弘肇取代州，殺其刺史王暉。

translations.literal: Military inspector Shi Hongzhao took Dai prefecture and killed its prefect Wang Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hongzhao of the military inspectorate seized Dai prefecture and executed the prefect Wang Hui.

sentences.zh: 晉州將藥可儔殺守將駱從朗及括錢使、諫議大夫趙熙來歸。

translations.literal: Jinzhou general Yao Ketal killed garrison commander Luo Conglang, the money-levying commissioner, and remonstrance grandee Zhao Xi, and came to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Ketal, a Jinzhou officer, killed the garrison commander Luo Conglang, the tax-enforcement commissioner, and remonstrance grandee Zhao Xi, then submitted the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，陜州留後趙暉、潞州留後王守恩來歸。

translations.literal: On xinsi, Shanzhou regent Zhao Hui and Luzhou regent Wang Shouen came to submit.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi Zhao Hui, regent of Shanzhou, and Wang Shouen, regent of Luzhou, submitted.

sentences.zh: 三月丙戌朔，蠲河東雜稅。

translations.literal: On bingxu, the new moon of the third month, miscellaneous taxes in Hedong were remitted.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingxu new moon of the third month miscellaneous levies in Hedong were abolished.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，延州軍亂，逐其節度使周密。

translations.literal: On xinmao the Yanzhou army mutinied and drove out its military commissioner Zhou Mi.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao troops at Yanzhou rebelled and expelled Military Commissioner Zhou Mi.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，丹州指揮使高彥詢以其州來歸。

translations.literal: On renchen, Danzhou commander Gao Yanxun submitted his prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen Gao Yanxun, commander of Danzhou, brought his prefecture over.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，契丹遁，以其將蕭翰為宣武軍節度使守汴州。

translations.literal: On renyin the Khitan withdrew, leaving their general Xiao Han as military commissioner of Xuanwu to hold Bianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin the Khitan pulled back, leaving Xiao Han as military commissioner of Xuanwu to guard Bianzhou.

sentences.zh: 夏四月己未，右都押衙楊邠為樞密使，蕃漢兵馬都孔目官郭威權樞密副使。

translations.literal: In the fourth month, summer, on jiwei, Right Chief Adjutant Yang Bin was made Privy Councilor and Fan-Han horse-and-foot chief clerk Guo Wei acting Vice Privy Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei in the fourth month Yang Bin, right chief adjutant, became Privy Councilor, and Guo Wei, chief clerk for Fan and Han horse troops, acting Vice Privy Councilor.

sentences.zh: 契丹陷相州，殺梁暉。

translations.literal: The Khitan captured Xiangzhou and killed Liang Hui.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan took Xiang prefecture and killed Liang Hui.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，立魏國夫人李氏為皇后。

translations.literal: On guihai Lady Li of Wei was established as empress.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai Lady Li of Wei was made empress.

sentences.zh: 甲子，河東節度判官蘇逢吉、觀察推官蘇禹珪為中書侍郎、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: On jiazi, Hedong military judge Su Fengji and observation push official Su Yugui were made Vice Directors of the Secretariat and Associate Grand Councilors.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi Su Fengji, military judge of Hedong, and Su Yugui, observation push official, became Vice Directors of the Secretariat and Associate Grand Councilors.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，侍衛親軍步軍都指揮使史弘肇取潞州。

translations.literal: On yichou, Imperial Guard foot commander Shi Hongzhao took Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou Shi Hongzhao, commander of the Imperial Guard foot corps, seized Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，奉國指揮使武行德以河陽來歸。

translations.literal: On wuchen, Fengguo commander Wu Xingde submitted Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen Wu Xingde of Fengguo brought Heyang over.

sentences.zh: 史弘肇取澤州。

translations.literal: Shi Hongzhao took Ze prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hongzhao took Ze prefecture.

sentences.zh: 丙子，契丹耶律德光卒於欒城，契丹入於鎮州。

translations.literal: On bingzi Yelü Deguang died at Luancheng; the Khitan entered Zhenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi Yelü Deguang died at Luancheng, and the Khitan fell back on Zhenzhou.

sentences.zh: 五月甲午，太原尹劉崇為北京留守。

translations.literal: On jiawu of the fifth month, Taiyuan Magistrate Liu Chong was made regent of the Northern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu in the fifth month Liu Chong, magistrate of Taiyuan, was named regent of the Northern Capital.

sentences.zh: 丙申，如東京。

translations.literal: On bingwu he proceeded to the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu the emperor set out for the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 蕭翰遁歸於契丹，以郇國公李從益知南朝軍國事。

translations.literal: Xiao Han fled back to the Khitan and made Li Congyi, Prince of Ye, oversee military and state affairs of the Southern Court.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Han fled to the Khitan and installed Li Congyi, Prince of Ye, to manage the Southern Court’s armies and administration.

sentences.zh: 戊申，次絳州，刺史李從朗來歸。

translations.literal: On wushen he halted at Jiang prefecture; Prefect Li Conglang submitted.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen the court paused at Jiang prefecture, where Prefect Li Conglang submitted.

sentences.zh: 六月丙辰，次河陽，殺李從益及其母於京師。

translations.literal: On bingchen of the sixth month he halted at Heyang; Li Congyi and his mother were put to death at the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen of the sixth month the march stopped at Heyang while Li Congyi and his mother were executed in the capital.

sentences.zh: 甲子，至自太原。

translations.literal: On jiazi he arrived, having come from Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi the emperor entered the capital from Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，改國號漢，赦罪人、蠲民稅。

translations.literal: On wuchen the state name was changed to Han; criminals were amnestied and the people’s taxes remitted.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen the dynasty took the name Han, granted a general amnesty, and cut levies on the people.

sentences.zh: 于闐遣使者來。

translations.literal: Khotan sent envoys.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys arrived from Khotan.

sentences.zh: 是夏，劉句薨。

translations.literal: That summer Liu Ju died.
translations.idiomatic: That summer Liu Ju died.

sentences.zh: 秋閏七月乙丑，禁造契丹服器。

translations.literal: In the intercalary seventh month of autumn, on yichou, making Khitan dress and vessels was forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou in the intercalary seventh month the court forbade the manufacture of Khitan garments and gear.

sentences.zh: 天雄軍節度使杜重威反，天平軍節度使高行周為鄴都行營都部署以討之。

translations.literal: Tianxiong military commissioner Du Chongwei rebelled; Tianping military commissioner Gao Xingzhou was made overall commander of the Yedu campaign headquarters to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: Du Chongwei, military commissioner of Tianxiong, rebelled. Gao Xingzhou of Tianping was appointed overall commander of the Yedu campaign to crush him.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，追尊祖考為皇帝，妣為皇后：高祖湍謚曰明元，廟號文祖，祖妣李氏謚曰明貞；

translations.literal: On gengchen the emperor’s forebears were posthumously honored as emperors and their consorts as empresses: great-grandfather Tuan, posthumous name Mingyuan, temple name Wenzu; great-grandmother Lady Li, posthumous name Mingzhen;
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen forebears were raised posthumously—emperors and their consorts empresses: great-grandfather Tuan received the temple name Wenzu and posthumous title Mingyuan; his consort Lady Li, Mingzhen;

sentences.zh: 曾祖昂謚曰恭僖，廟號德祖，祖妣楊氏謚曰恭惠；

translations.literal: great-great-grandfather Ang, posthumous name Gongxi, temple name Dezu; his consort Lady Yang, posthumous name Gonghui;
translations.idiomatic: great-great-grandfather Ang, Dezu and Gongxi; his consort Lady Yang, Gonghui;

sentences.zh: 祖僎謚曰昭憲，廟號翼祖，祖妣李氏謚曰昭穆；

translations.literal: grandfather Juan, posthumous name Zhaoxian, temple name Yizu; his consort Lady Li, posthumous name Zhaomu;
translations.idiomatic: grandfather Juan, Yizu and Zhaoxian; his consort Lady Li, Zhaomu;

sentences.zh: 考典謚曰章聖，廟號顯祖，妣安氏謚曰章懿。

translations.literal: father Dian, posthumous name Zhangsheng, temple name Xianzu; mother Lady An, posthumous name Zhangyi.
translations.idiomatic: father Dian, Xianzu and Zhangsheng; mother Lady An, Zhangyi.

sentences.zh: 以漢高皇帝為高祖，光武皇帝為世祖，皆不祧。

translations.literal: Han’s Emperor Gaozu was taken as dynastic Gaozu and Guangwu as dynastic Shizu—neither was removed from the temple line.
translations.idiomatic: The Han Emperor Gaozu and Emperor Guangwu were enshrined as the dynasty’s Gaozu and Shizu, neither displaced from the ancestral line.

sentences.zh: 八月，護聖指揮使白再榮逐契丹，以鎮州來歸。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Husheng commander Bai Zairong drove out the Khitan and submitted Zhenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Bai Zairong of Husheng expelled the Khitan and brought Zhen prefecture over.

sentences.zh: 丙申，安國軍節度使薛懷讓殺契丹之將劉鐸，入於邢州。

translations.literal: On bingwu, Anguo military commissioner Xue Huairang killed the Khitan general Liu Duo and entered Xingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu Xue Huairang of Anguo killed the Khitan commander Liu Duo and took Xing prefecture.

sentences.zh: 九月甲戌，吏部尚書竇貞固守司空兼門下侍郎，翰林學士、中書舍人李濤為中書侍郎：同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: On jiaxu, Minister of Personnel Dou Zhengu continued as Minister of Works and Vice Director of the Secretariat; Hanlin academician and Secretariat drafting officer Li Tao was made Vice Director of the Secretariat: both Associate Grand Councilors.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu Dou Zhengu of the Ministry of Personnel kept the Ministry of Works and the Vice Directorship of the Secretariat; Li Tao, Hanlin academician and drafting officer, became Vice Director—both Associate Grand Councilors.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，北征。

translations.literal: On gengchen the northern campaign set out.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen the emperor marched north.

sentences.zh: 冬十月甲申，次韋城，赦河北。

translations.literal: On jiashen of the tenth month, winter, the court halted at Weicheng and amnestied Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen in the tenth month the army encamped at Weicheng and proclaimed an amnesty for Hebei.

sentences.zh: 十一月壬申，杜重威降。

translations.literal: On renshen of the eleventh month Du Chongwei surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen of the eleventh month Du Chongwei surrendered.

sentences.zh: 十二月癸巳，至自鄴都。

translations.literal: On guisi he returned from Yedu.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi the emperor came back from Yedu.

sentences.zh: 乾祐元年春正月乙卯，大赦，改元。

translations.literal: On yimao, first month of spring in Qianyou 1, a great amnesty was proclaimed and the era name changed.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao in the first month of Qianyou 1 the court proclaimed a great amnesty and changed the era name.

sentences.zh: 己未，更名暠。

translations.literal: On jiwei he was renamed Gao.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei Gaozu took the taboo name Gao.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，皇帝崩於萬歲殿。

translations.literal: On dingchou the emperor died in the Hall of Myriad Years.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou the emperor died in the Hall of Myriad Years.

sentences.zh: 乾祐元年二月辛巳，封承祐周王。

translations.literal: On xinsi of the second month of Qianyou 1, Chengyou was enfeoffed Prince of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi in the second month of Qianyou 1 Chengyou was enfeoffed as Prince of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 是日，皇帝即位於柩前。

translations.literal: That day the emperor ascended the throne before the coffin.
translations.idiomatic: That same day the Hidden Emperor took the throne before the bier.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，右衛大將軍、鳳翔巡檢使王景崇及蜀人戰於大散關，敗之。

translations.literal: On renchen, Right Guard senior general and Fengxiang inspection commissioner Wang Jingchong fought the Shu at Dasanguan and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen Wang Jingchong, senior general of the Right Guard and Fengxiang inspection commissioner, met the Shu at Dasanguan and routed them.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，大赦。

translations.literal: On guisi a great amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi the court proclaimed a great amnesty.

sentences.zh: 三月壬戌，竇貞固為大行皇帝山陵使，吏部侍郎段希堯為副，太常卿張昭為禮儀使，兵部侍郎盧價為鹵簿使，御史中丞邊蔚為儀仗使。

translations.literal: On renxu, Dou Zhengu was made director for the late emperor’s tomb, Vice Minister of Personnel Duan Xiyao deputy, Director of Ceremonies Zhang Zhao ritual commissioner, Vice Minister of War Lu Jia escort commissioner, and Censor-in-Chief Bian Wei arms commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu Dou Zhengu directed the late emperor’s tomb works, with Duan Xiyao of the Ministry of Personnel as deputy; Zhang Zhao oversaw the rites, Lu Jia the procession, and Censor-in-Chief Bian Wei the honor guard.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，李濤罷。

translations.literal: On dingchou Li Tao was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou Li Tao left office.

sentences.zh: 護國軍節度使李守貞反，陷潼關。

translations.literal: Huguo military commissioner Li Shouzhen rebelled and seized Tong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shouzhen, military commissioner of Huguo, rebelled and took Tong Pass.

sentences.zh: 夏四月辛巳，陜州兵馬都監王玉克潼關。

translations.literal: On xinsi of the fourth month, summer, Shanzhou horse-and-foot inspector Wang Yu took Tong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi in the fourth month Wang Yu, Shanzhou’s horse-and-foot inspector, recovered Tong Pass.

sentences.zh: 壬午，永興軍將趙思綰叛附於李守貞，客省使王峻帥師屯於關西。

translations.literal: On renwu, Yongxing officer Zhao Sizhen rebelled and joined Li Shouzhen; guest commissioner Wang Jun led troops stationed west of the Pass.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu Zhao Sizhen of Yongxing mutinied to Li Shouzhen’s side, and Wang Jun, guest commissioner, encamped with an army west of the Pass.

sentences.zh: 楊邠為中書侍郎兼吏部尚書、同中書門下平章事，郭威為樞密使，鎮寧軍節度使郭從義為永興軍兵馬都部署。

translations.literal: Yang Bin was made Vice Director of the Secretariat and concurrently Minister of Personnel, Associate Grand Councilor; Guo Wei became Privy Councilor; Zhenning military commissioner Guo Congyi was made Yongxing horse-and-foot deployment commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Bin became Vice Director of the Secretariat and Minister of Personnel, Associate Grand Councilor; Guo Wei, Privy Councilor; and Guo Congyi of Zhenning, deployment commissioner for Yongxing horse and foot.

sentences.zh: 戊子，保義軍節度使白文珂為河中兵馬都部署。

translations.literal: On wuzi, Baoyi military commissioner Bai Wenke was made overall deployment commissioner for Hezhong horse and foot.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi Bai Wenke of Baoyi was named overall deployment commissioner for the Hezhong armies.

sentences.zh: 河決原武。

translations.literal: The Yellow River broke its banks at Yuanwu.
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow River burst its dikes at Yuanwu.

sentences.zh: 五月己未，回鶻遣使者來。

translations.literal: On jiwei of the fifth month Uyghur envoys arrived.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei in the fifth month envoys came from the Uyghurs.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，魏州內黃民武進妻一產三男子。

translations.literal: On yihai, the wife of Wu Jin of Neihuang in Weizhou bore three sons in one birth.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai the wife of Wu Jin of Neihuang in Weizhou gave birth to triplet sons.

sentences.zh: 河決滑州魚池。

translations.literal: The Yellow River broke its banks at Yuchi in Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow River burst its dikes at Yuchi in Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 旱，蝗。

translations.literal: Drought; locusts.
translations.idiomatic: Drought struck, and locusts swarmed.

sentences.zh: 秋七月戊申朔，彰德軍節度使王繼弘殺其判官張易。

translations.literal: On wushen, new moon of the seventh month, autumn, Zhangde military commissioner Wang Jihong killed his judge Zhang Yi.
translations.idiomatic: On the wushen new moon of the seventh month Wang Jihong, military commissioner of Zhangde, killed his administrative judge Zhang Yi.

sentences.zh: 翙鵒食蝗。

translations.literal: Sacred ibises ate the locusts.
translations.idiomatic: Sacred ibises devoured the locusts.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，禁捕翙鵒。

translations.literal: On bingchen the hunting of sacred ibises was forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen the court forbade the taking of sacred ibises.

sentences.zh: 庚申，郭威同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: On gengshen Guo Wei became Associate Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen Guo Wei was made Associate Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，契丹鄚州刺史王彥徽來奔。

translations.literal: On guihai Wang Yanhui, prefect of Mo in Khitan territory, came over in flight.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai Wang Yanhui, Khitan prefect of Mo, defected to Han.

sentences.zh: 庚午，殺成德軍副使張鵬。

translations.literal: On gengwu Zhang Peng, deputy commissioner of Chengde, was executed.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu Zhang Peng, deputy commissioner of Chengde, was put to death.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，王景崇叛附於李守貞。

translations.literal: On yihai Wang Jingchong rebelled and joined Li Shouzhen.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai Wang Jingchong turned rebel and went over to Li Shouzhen.

sentences.zh: 八月壬午，郭威討李守貞。

translations.literal: On renwu of the eighth month Guo Wei campaigned against Li Shouzhen.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu in the eighth month Guo Wei marched to suppress Li Shouzhen.

sentences.zh: 九月，西面行營都虞候尚弘遷及趙思綰戰，敗績。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, Western Campaign deputy commander Shang Hongqian fought Zhao Sizhen and was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Shang Hongqian, deputy of the Western Campaign, met Zhao Sizhen and suffered defeat.

sentences.zh: 冬十月甲申，吐蕃使斯漫篤蘭氈藥斯來。

translations.literal: On jiashen of the tenth month, winter, the Tibetan envoy Simandulan Zhan Yaosi came.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen in the tenth month a Tibetan mission led by Simandulan Zhan Yaosi arrived.

sentences.zh: 十一月甲寅，殺太子太傅李崧，滅其族。

translations.literal: On jiayin of the eleventh month Li Song, Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, was executed and his clan exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin Li Song, Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, was executed and his entire clan wiped out.

sentences.zh: 壬申，葬睿文聖武昭肅孝皇帝於睿陵。

translations.literal: On renshen the Sagely Literary, Sagely Military, Resplendent and Solemn, Filial Emperor was buried at Ruiling.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen Gaozu, the Sagely Literary, Sagely Military, Resplendent and Solemn, Filial Emperor, was laid to rest at Ruiling.

sentences.zh: 十二月己卯，彰武軍節度使高允權殺太子太師致仕劉景巖。

translations.literal: On jimao of the twelfth month, Zhangwu military commissioner Gao Yunquan killed the retired Grand Preceptor Liu Jingyan.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao Gao Yunquan of Zhangwu murdered Liu Jingyan, the retired Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 二年春正月乙巳朔，赦囚。

translations.literal: On yisi, new moon of the first month of spring in year 2, prisoners were amnestied.
translations.idiomatic: On the yisi new moon of the second year the court amnestied prisoners.

sentences.zh: 二月丙子，蠲民紐配租。

translations.literal: On bingzi the people’s supplementary cloth levies were remitted.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi supplemental cloth levies on the people were abolished.

sentences.zh: 夏五月，李守貞之將周光遜降。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of summer, Zhou Guangxun, a general of Li Shouzhen, surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Zhou Guangxun, an officer under Li Shouzhen, surrendered.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，趙思綰降。

translations.literal: On yichou Zhao Sizhen surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou Zhao Sizhen surrendered.

sentences.zh: 六月辛卯，回鶻首領楊彥珣來。

translations.literal: On xinmao of the sixth month, Uyghur chieftain Yang Yanxun came.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao in the sixth month the Uyghur chieftain Yang Yanxun arrived.

sentences.zh: 西涼府遣使者來。

translations.literal: The Western Liang prefectural seat sent envoys.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys arrived from the Western Liang prefectural administration.

sentences.zh: 蝗。

translations.literal: Locusts.
translations.idiomatic: Locusts swarmed.

sentences.zh: 秋七月丁巳，郭威殺華州留後趙思綰於京兆。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of autumn, on dingsi, Guo Wei killed Zhao Sizhen, rear commander of Huazhou, at Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi in the seventh month of autumn Guo Wei executed Zhao Sizhen, rear commander of Huazhou, at Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 甲子，克河中。

translations.literal: On jiazi Hezhong was taken.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi Hezhong fell.

sentences.zh: 八月，郭從義殺前永興巡檢喬守溫。

translations.literal: In the eighth month Guo Congyi killed Qiao Shouwen, former inspector of Yongxing.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Guo Congyi put to death Qiao Shouwen, the former Yongxing inspector.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，郭威使來獻俘。

translations.literal: On bingxu Guo Wei’s envoy came presenting captives.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu an envoy from Guo Wei arrived with prisoners for the court.

sentences.zh: 冬十月，契丹寇趙、魏，群臣進添都馬。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of winter the Khitan raided Zhao and Wei; the ministers presented additional capital horses.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Khitan forces struck Zhao and Wei prefectures, and the ministers offered extra horses for the capital guard.

sentences.zh: 契丹陷內丘。

translations.literal: The Khitan took Neiqiu.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan seized Neiqiu.

sentences.zh: 己丑，郭威及宣徽南院使王峻伐契丹。

translations.literal: On jichou Guo Wei and Wang Jun, commissioner of the Southern Bureau of the Palace Secretariat, campaigned against the Khitan.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou Guo Wei marched against the Khitan with Wang Jun, commissioner of the Southern Bureau of the Palace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 十一月，契丹遁。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month the Khitan withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month the Khitan pulled back.

sentences.zh: 三年春正月，西面行營都部署趙暉克鳳翔。

translations.literal: In the third year, spring, in the first month Zhao Hui, overall deployment commander of the Western Campaign, took Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, in the first month of spring, Zhao Hui, overall commander of the western field army, captured Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 丙午，郭威進添都馬。

translations.literal: On bingwu Guo Wei presented additional capital horses.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu Guo Wei offered extra horses for the capital guard.

sentences.zh: 壬子，趙暉獻馘俘。

translations.literal: On renzi Zhao Hui presented severed heads and captives.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi Zhao Hui presented heads and prisoners taken in battle.

sentences.zh: 二月甲戌，旌表潁州汝陰民麹溫門閭。

translations.literal: On jiaxu of the second month the household gate of Qu Wen, a commoner of Runan in Ying prefecture, was marked with honor.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu of the second month the court honored the household gate of Qu Wen of Runan in Ying prefecture for exemplary conduct.

sentences.zh: 三月己酉，寒食，望祭於南禦園。

translations.literal: On jiyou of the third month, on Cold Food Day, he performed look-toward sacrifice at the Southern Imperial Garden.
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou of the third month, on Cold Food Day, the emperor made offering by gazing toward the Southern Imperial Garden.

sentences.zh: 夏四月壬午，郭威以樞密使為天雄軍節度使。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of summer, on renchen, Guo Wei the Privy Councilor was made military commissioner of Tianxiong.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen in the fourth month Guo Wei, Privy Councilor, was appointed military commissioner of Tianxiong.

sentences.zh: 六月癸卯，河決原武。

translations.literal: On guimao in the sixth month the river broke at Yuanwu.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao in the sixth month the Yellow River burst its dikes at Yuanwu.

sentences.zh: 秋八月，達靼來附。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of autumn the Dadan submitted.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month the Dadan tribes came over in submission.

sentences.zh: 冬十一月丙子，殺楊邠及侍衛親軍都指揮使史弘肇、三司使王章，皆滅其族。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of winter, on bingzi, Yang Bin was killed, together with Shi Hongzhao, commander of the palace personal army, and Wang Zhang, commissioner of the Three Departments—all their clans were exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi in the eleventh month Yang Bin was executed, along with Shi Hongzhao, commander of the palace guards, and Wang Zhang, commissioner of the Three Departments; every clan of the three was wiped out.

sentences.zh: 郭威反。

translations.literal: Guo Wei rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Wei rose in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，義成軍節度使宋延渥叛附於威。

translations.literal: On gengchen Song Yanwo, military commissioner of Yicheng, rebelled and joined Guo Wei.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen Song Yanwo of Yicheng turned rebel and went over to Guo Wei.

sentences.zh: 壬午，威犯封丘，泰寧軍節度使慕容彥超軍於七里店。

translations.literal: On renwu Guo Wei attacked Fengqiu; Murong Yanchao, military commissioner of Taining, encamped at Qilidian.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu Guo Wei advanced on Fengqiu while Murong Yanchao of Taining drew up his army at Qilidian.

sentences.zh: 癸未，勞軍於北郊。

translations.literal: On guimao the emperor reviewed troops at the northern suburbs.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao the emperor reviewed the army in the northern suburbs.

sentences.zh: 甲申，勞軍於劉子陂。

translations.literal: On jiashen he reviewed troops at Liuzipo.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen he reviewed the army again at Liuzipo.

sentences.zh: 慕容彥超及郭威戰，敗績，開封尹侯益叛降於威。

translations.literal: Murong Yanchao fought Guo Wei and was defeated; Hou Yi, governor of Kaifeng, rebelled and surrendered to Guo Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Yanchao met Guo Wei in battle and was routed; Hou Yi, governor of Kaifeng, defected to the rebel side.

sentences.zh: 郭允明反。

translations.literal: Guo Yunming rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Yunming rose in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，皇帝崩，蘇逢吉自殺。

translations.literal: On yiyou the emperor died; Su Fengji killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou the emperor died; Su Fengji took his own life.

sentences.zh: 漢亡。

translations.literal: Han perished.
translations.idiomatic: Han fell.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 人君即位稱元年，常事爾，古不以為重也。

translations.literal: When a lord takes the throne and calls it year one of his reign, it is an ordinary matter; antiquity did not treat it as weighty.
translations.idiomatic: For a ruler to take the throne and name the first year of his reign was routine; the ancients did not make much of it.

sentences.zh: 孔子未修《春秋》，其前固已如此，雖暴君昏主，妄庸之史，其記事先後遠近，莫不以歲月一二數之，乃理之自然也。

translations.literal: Before Confucius edited the Spring and Autumn Annals it was already so; even tyrants and muddle-headed rulers, with worthless chroniclers, recorded events in near and far order, all counting by one or two year-numbers—it is the natural course of reason.
translations.idiomatic: Even before Confucius edited the Spring and Autumn Annals the practice was fixed: tyrants and foolish kings, with incompetent scribes, still ordered events near and far by a year or two of numbering—it is simply how reason arranges things.

sentences.zh: 其謂一為元，亦未嘗有法，蓋古人之語爾。

translations.literal: That “one” should be called the origin was never really a fixed law; it is only how the ancients spoke.
translations.idiomatic: The notion that the first year should be called the “origin” was never a binding rule—only an old way of speaking.

sentences.zh: 及後世曲學之士，始謂孔子書「元年」為《春秋》大法，遂以改元為重事。

translations.literal: Only later did pedantic scholars begin to say that Confucius’s writing of “year one” in the Spring and Autumn was the great principle of that classic, and so they made changing the reign title a weighty affair.
translations.idiomatic: Only later did narrow scholars decide that Confucius’s “year one” in the Spring and Autumn Annals was the classic’s grand law, and they turned the change of reign title into a solemn matter.

sentences.zh: 自漢以後，又名年以建元，而正偽紛雜，稱號遂多，不勝其紀也。

translations.literal: From Han onward reigns were also named by “establishing the origin,” and orthodoxy and usurpation became tangled until titles multiplied beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: After Han, rulers also named their eras by “establishing the origin,” and with legitimacy and usurpation hopelessly mixed, reign titles multiplied until no one could keep track.

sentences.zh: 五代，亂世也，其事無法而不合於理者多矣，皆不足道也。

translations.literal: The Five Dynasties were an age of disorder; many of their affairs lacked proper method and accorded ill with reason—they are not worth discussing.
translations.idiomatic: The Five Dynasties were a time of chaos; much that they did was lawless and unreasonable, and hardly merits discussion.

sentences.zh: 至其年號乖錯以惑後世，則不可以不明。

translations.literal: Yet where their reign titles were twisted and wrong and would mislead later ages, that cannot be left unclear.
translations.idiomatic: But where their era names were twisted so as to confuse posterity, the record must be set straight.

sentences.zh: 初，梁太祖以乾化二年遇弒，明年，末帝已誅友珪，黜其鳳歷之號，復稱乾化三年，尚為有說。

translations.literal: At first Liang Taizu was assassinated in the second year of Qianhua; the next year the Last Emperor had You Gui executed, set aside his Fengli reign title, and restored the third year of Qianhua—there was still some rationale in that.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang Taizu was murdered in Qianhua 2, the Last Emperor the next year killed You Gui, abolished his Fengli era, and returned to Qianhua 3—one could still find a reason for that.

sentences.zh: 至漢高祖建國，黜晉出帝開運四年，復稱天福十二年者，何哉？

translations.literal: But when Han Gaozu founded his state, set aside the Outgoing Emperor’s fourth Kaiyun year, and revived the twelfth Tianfu year—why?
translations.idiomatic: When Han Gaozu founded the dynasty, cast aside the Outgoing Emperor’s Kaiyun 4, and revived Tianfu 12—what was that for?

sentences.zh: 蓋以其愛憎之私爾。

translations.literal: It was merely the working of private love and hate.
translations.idiomatic: Nothing but private favor and spite.

sentences.zh: 方出帝時，漢高祖居太原，常憤憤下視晉，而晉亦陽優禮之，幸而未見其隙。

translations.literal: While the Outgoing Emperor still reigned, Han Gaozu held Taiyuan and often gazed down on Jin with resentment; Jin for its part treated him with outward courtesy, and by luck never found a pretext against him.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Outgoing Emperor, Liu Zhiyuan at Taiyuan often looked on Jin with smoldering anger, while Jin feigned courtesy toward him and, by luck, never caught him out.

sentences.zh: 及契丹滅晉，漢未嘗有赴難之意。

translations.literal: When the Khitan destroyed Jin, Han never showed the least will to go to its rescue.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan overthrew Jin, Han showed not the slightest intention of riding to its aid.

sentences.zh: 出帝已北遷，方陽以兵聲言追之，至土門而還。

translations.literal: After the Outgoing Emperor had been moved north, Han openly made a show of pursuing him with troops, yet turned back at Tumen Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Outgoing Emperor had been taken north, Han loudly claimed to be pursuing him with an army, then marched only as far as Tumen Pass and turned back.

sentences.zh: 及其即位改元，而黜開運之號，則其用心可知矣。

translations.literal: When he took the throne and changed the era, casting aside the Kaiyun title, his intent was plain enough.
translations.idiomatic: When he acceded and changed the era, erasing the Kaiyun name, his purpose was plain enough.

sentences.zh: 蓋其於出帝無復君臣之義，而幸禍以為利者，其素誌也，可勝嘆哉！

translations.literal: He had long since ceased to owe the Outgoing Emperor any bond of ruler and subject, and rejoiced in calamity for profit—that was his settled mind; how lamentable!
translations.idiomatic: Toward the Outgoing Emperor he no longer held any bond of ruler and subject, and welcomed disaster for gain—that had been his settled mind all along. The pity of it!

sentences.zh: 夫所謂有諸中必形於外者，其見於是乎！

translations.literal: What they call “what is within must show without”—was it not seen here!
translations.idiomatic: As the saying goes, what fills the heart must show in the face—was it not plain here?
